problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Projection Matrices, Linear Transformations and Their Properties

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
examples.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v} + t\mathbf{w}$, where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/bd8680b251ca871c0912f7aa85826bc705f022d12155fa1ddc73e2d01c30d2ca.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix $P_S = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T$ maps any vector $\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^n$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v}+t\mathbf{w}$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}.$ 
Hence, we have 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/af442d03acdc13db51c3ae53fcf250074e9adc2d4ed4bd2f52e6e76b5d4c2fe8.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 & 3 \\ -6 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
